details:
Q1: A scheduled scan has no OIDC-signed report. What should count as verified evidence before the scan runs the recovery path?
Choices:
A. Rebuild the report from the heal issue's own pipeline-written metadata: source repo and PR/issue, run IDs and fingerprint. Then re-check each run through the existing provenance gate: same repository, failed conclusion, allowed workflow path, linked to the source item. Recompute the fingerprint from the fetched job logs and require it to match the issue. Only then pass a separate auth value (for example `report_auth=reconstructed`) that only the recovery path accepts. Logs that cannot be read or have expired, or a mismatch, mean skip with nothing filed. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Don't change authentication. The scan only re-triggers the original reporter (re-dispatch review/autofix on the source PR) so a fresh OIDC-signed report arrives at the intake. This does not work when the source PR is closed or its head has moved.
C. Accept a heal issue as evidence on its own when it is pipeline-authored and has no marker, without re-reading any runs.
Q2: Which non-retryable reasons should be checked for recovery before the early exit (gap 2)?
Choices:
A. Only `conflict_resolver_sandbox_path_unsupported` and `conflict_resolver_sandbox_support_missing`. `conflict_resolver_sandbox_path_host_only` keeps its #6745/#6756 manual-merge outcome and never becomes a heal issue, even as a replacement. (RECOMMENDED)
B. All three reasons in `NON_RETRYABLE_FAILURE_REASONS`, including the host-only stop. This overrides #6756's "never becomes a heal issue" rule for recovery replacements.
Q3: For an authenticated non-retryable report that is eligible for recovery, should the existing non-retryable PR handling still run after the replacement is created? That handling is the `ai:workflow-heal-non-retryable:v1` comment, `ai:needs-human`, and the WARNING.
Choices:
A. Recovery only. Create the scoped replacement, close the original, and skip the PR diagnosis comment and label for this report.
B. Both. Run recovery first, then the existing non-retryable PR handling unchanged. Its per-pr/head/reason dedup still applies. (RECOMMENDED)
Assumptions I made (not asked):
- Planning picks the scan's trigger. The natural choice is a `schedule:` on `workflow-failure-heal-intake.yml`, which already has the shared `workflow-failure-heal-intake` concurrency group.
- The scan has a per-tick cap and stays behind the `HEAL_SCOPE_RECOVERY_ENABLED` switch.
Missing context: I could not check GitHub to see whether #7082 is still open or whether its failed-run logs are still retained.
